programme_name_exact: MSc in Business Intelligence and Data Analytics
entry_requirement_note: Admissions Requirements: "Bachelor's degree and transcripts from an accredited program. In terms of GPA, we expect 2:2 and above from UK schools, 3.0 and above from US schools, and 6.5 and above or the equivalent from Cypriot and Greek Universities and colleges." Also: "Satisfactory quantitative skills as evidenced by the quantitative courses they have taken during their Bachelor's degree study." No credit volume and no minimum duration of prior study is published; a 3-year 180-ECTS licence is not excluded by the wording, but the quantitative-coursework check is an individual assessment.

institution: American University of Beirut - Mediterraneo (AUB Mediterraneo)
programme_name_exact: Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSBA)
entry_requirement_note: AMBIGUOUS - no prior-degree rule published. The official Graduate Admissions page lists only documentary requirements: "Official transcripts from all institutions previously attended providing a complete record of study. Statement of purpose. Resume or CV. English language requirement (upon admission and prior to matriculation)." It states no required degree type, credit volume, duration or GPA, and the MSBA programme page carries no admission section. Prior credit volume acceptable for entry cannot be established from published sources; applicant must ask admissions directly.

programme_name_exact: MSc in e-Business and Digital Marketing
entry_requirement_note: Who can apply: "An undergraduate University degree in Engineering, Science, Informatics, Economics & Business Administration as well as from Technological Educational Institutes in related subject areas, in Greece or a recognized Higher Education Institution from abroad." Key-facts box: "An undergraduate degree from an accredited University, preferably in Engineering, Science, Informatics, Economics & Business Administration." No ECTS floor and no minimum number of years is published. Foreign institutions must be on the DOATAP recognised list, and enrolment requires an authenticated degree (validation via a Greek consulate/embassy, can take 3+ months). Greek first-cycle degrees are normally 4 years / 240 ECTS, but the programme publishes no credit minimum, so 180 ECTS is neither accepted nor excluded in writing.

Who can apply: "An undergraduate degree from a Higher Education Institution in Greece or a recognized Higher Education Institution from abroad. STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) degrees are deemed to be compatible with the programme. However, other degrees are also considered in case of solid background in statistics/mathematics and good knowledge of fundamental concepts of databases and programming." No ECTS floor and no minimum duration published. Foreign institution must be DOATAP-recognised; enrolment requires an authenticated degree. Subject-specific expectation (statistics/mathematics, databases, programming) is assessed individually rather than by credit count.

institution: Athens University of Economics and Business
entry_requirement_note: Admission requirement: "An undergraduate degree from a formally recognized Greek or foreign University." Application process adds: "In case of foreign degrees, applicants must submit a recognition certificate from the National Academic Recognition Information Center" (DOATAP). No ECTS floor, no minimum years, no subject restriction published. English C2 for full-time / C1 for part-time; part-time also needs 2 years work experience. Whether a 180-ECTS Tunisian licence qualifies turns entirely on the DOATAP/AUEB academic assessment of the foreign title.

institution: Athens University of Economics and Business
programme_name_exact: MSc in AI and Data Science
entry_requirement_note: The official Admission Requirements page lists required documents only, including "Copy of all university degrees/diplomas received" and "Certificate of equivalence for degrees from foreign Universities, issued by DOATAP/Hellenic NARIC", plus proof of English at C2, two recommendation letters and CV. No accepted-degree list, no ECTS floor and no minimum years of prior study are published on the page (it defers to the annual Call for Applications). Admission of a 180-ECTS licence therefore depends on the DOATAP/Hellenic NARIC equivalence certificate.

institution: Athens University of Economics and Business
entry_requirement_note: Applicants' Profile & Requirements: "All fields will be considered, but management science, business administration, mathematics, physics, statistics, engineering and computer science seem a natural fit for the program"; applicants should have "basic IT concepts, such as programming and database management". Requirements are listed as "Bachelor's degree, Recommendation letters, Curriculum Vitae, Verified advanced or excellent command of the English language (C1/C2 level)". No ECTS floor or minimum years published. Under Greek law 4957/2022 AUEB itself academically assesses foreign titles against the DOATAP national registries, so a 180-ECTS licence is subject to individual assessment.

programme_name_exact: Master of Science (MSc) in Business Analytics
entry_requirement_note: "Level 8 honours degree with a minimum 2.2 in a relevant area. Cognate areas include business, IT, finance, economics, mathematics, statistics and related fields." FAQ adds: "Applicants normally need a Level 8 honours bachelor's degree with a minimum 2.2 in a relevant area. Non-cognate applicants may be considered with three to five years' business analytics experience." No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. Business Intelligence is a cognate area, so the subject fit is satisfied.

"Applicants must hold a minimum of a bachelor's degree (NFQ Level 8) (or equivalent) with a minimum of a second-class honours, grade 2 (2:2) in a discipline which includes quantitative techniques as part of the degree (including the ability to undertake statistical analysis of data). Examples of such degrees include business studies, management science, economics, finance, accounting, engineering, mathematics, physics, computer science and other sciences." RPL route exists for applicants without a primary degree who have 10+ years relevant experience. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment.

"Applicants should hold a bachelor's degree (NFQ Level 8) with at least a second-class honours, grade 2 (2:2) in a relevant discipline e.g. business, finance, economics mathematics, engineering, computer science, etc." UL's general postgraduate rule is a "first or second class Level 8 honours degree (NFQ or other internationally recognised equivalents) in a relevant or appropriate subject". No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. NOTE: UL publishes a country-by-country international entry table but it contains NO Tunisia row (nearest North African entry is Libya); for several countries that table does demand a four-year degree and for China explicitly states "We do not accept three-year degrees", so a Tunisian 180-ECTS licence must be individually assessed.

"Normally a H2.1 degree (NFQ Level 8 or equivalent). However, candidates with a H2.2 honours degree and who have a minimum of 2 years relevant work experience will also be considered." Subject requirement: "The qualification must include an element of quantitative techniques, for example, graduates of Business Studies, Engineering, Computer Science, other Sciences, Mathematics or other courses that have some quantitative content." No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment.

"Applicants must have a Second Class Honours Grade 2 in a primary honours degree (NFQ, Level 8). The qualification must include one module in a quantitative area, for example, Finance, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Computer Science, or other Sciences." RPL considered for applicants with 3 years professional industry experience. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. NOTE: UCC publishes per-country postgraduate comparison tables (Africa/Middle East/India section) but Tunisia is NOT listed among them.

programme_name_exact: MSc in Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence
entry_requirement_note: "An NFQ Level 8 2.1 Honours degree (or higher) in a relevant discipline, such as Business, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or an equivalent international qualification." Plus: "Applications from candidates with a 2.2 may be considered in exceptional circumstances... reviewed on a case-by-case basis." No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment.

programme_name_exact: Business Analytics and AI for Management (M.Sc.)
entry_requirement_note: "Applicants typically have a strong academic background, normally a minimum 2.1 honours degree or international equivalent, in a quantitative subject such as Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science or Business." Trinity's general postgraduate rule: applicants must "hold at least a 2.1 honors degree from an Irish university or equivalent result from a university in another country." No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. NOTE: Trinity DOES publish a dedicated Tunisia country page (https://www.tcd.ie/study/country/tunisia/) but it repeats only the generic "2.1 honours degree or equivalent" line for postgraduate entry and maps no Tunisian qualification (Licence/Maitrise) to it; it refers Tunisian applicants to a named regional manager for credential assessment.

"A minimum second class honours primary degree (or equivalent) which includes quantitative techniques. For example graduates of Engineering, Computer Science, other Sciences. For Business studies background students, applicants need to have a background in MIS-Management Information Systems subjects, Maths or other quantitative courses. A student may be asked to undertake the GMAT or GRE at the Director's discretion." RPL may be awarded for admission and/or credit exemptions. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. NOTE: UCD publishes a Tunisia country page but it covers UNDERGRADUATE entry only (Baccalaureat-based) and gives no postgraduate mapping. On that same UCD Tunisia page UCD itself glosses NFQ Level 8 as "a 4-year Bachelor degree (NFQ Level 8)" - UCD's own confirmation that Irish Level 8 means four years / 240 ECTS.

programme_name_exact: Digital Media and Communications (MA, 1.5 Years or 3 Semesters)
entry_requirement_note: Admission Criteria, in full: "The minimum general requirement for admission to the post-graduate degree programme is a Bachelor Degree from a recognised university." No credit volume, no minimum duration, no subject restriction and no grade threshold is attached. A 180-ECTS 3-year licence satisfies this wording; the only variable is whether Esprit School of Business is treated as a recognised university. English: IELTS 6.5+ or equivalent (free NEPTON placement test accepted as substitute).

programme_name_exact: MSc Interaction Design (joint programme with Tallinn University)
entry_requirement_note: "A degree in a related field with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 6.5/10, or equivalent, from a recognized and accredited university." Related fields listed: Computer Science, Informatics, Design, Media Studies, Internet Studies, Social Sciences, Psychology, Education. No ECTS floor and no minimum duration of prior study is published. Conditional because the "related field" test is a discretionary subject assessment - Business Intelligence is not on the listed field list, though its informatics content may be argued.

Graduates Abroad category: "Graduates of departments of Universities from abroad in a discipline related to Computer Science. That is, a degree (or an international equivalent) is required in computer science or electrical and computer engineering or a numerate physical science discipline)." Grade floor: "A Bachelor's degree as described above, with a minimum requirement of a 6.5 grade (or the equivalent for different grading systems)" and "The minimum grade of the degree/diploma or first cycle must be at least equal to six (6) in the scale 0-10". No ECTS floor and no minimum years published. CRITICAL: "Master's degree is not awarded to a postgraduate student whose title of first-cycle studies (i.e. BSc.) from a foreign Institution has not been recognized by the Hellenic National Academic Recognition and Information Center (DOATAP), according to the Law 3328/2005 (A' 80)" - DOATAP recognition of the Tunisian licence is a condition of graduating, not merely of entry.

programme_name_exact: MA in Digital Media, Communication and Journalism
entry_requirement_note: "Holders of first cycle degrees (Bachelor's) are admitted to the Program and in particular graduates of the Departments of Journalism, Media or Communication, as well as graduates of humanities and social sciences." Formal requirement: "Hold a Bachelor's Degree (BA) from a Greek or a foreign university or advanced technological educational institution, at a 2.1 level or equivalent grade (eg. B, very good, etc) in one of the following disciplines Journalism, Communication, Advertising Marketing, Political, Social and Cultural Studies, Economics, Comparative, European and International Studies, History, Anthropology, Psychology, Sociology, Philosophy, Archeology, History of Arts and Foreign Languages." No ECTS floor or minimum years published. FLAG: Business Intelligence is not on the eligible discipline list; the nearest listed field is Economics, so subject eligibility is doubtful independently of credit volume.

Minimum entry requirements: "Undergraduate qualification of 2nd Class Honours or higher at Honours Degree level. Some prior experience in a cognate discipline is desirable." Alternative: "Applicants without an appropriate degree qualification may be considered provided they can demonstrate equivalent experience through our RPL (recognition of prior learning) process." No portfolio required. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment.

Entry requirements: "Students with a Level 8 qualification or RPL (to include completed postgraduate study in related Art and Design areas or postgraduate experience working in the animation industry)." A portfolio containing animation-related project proposals is mandatory. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. Note the portfolio, not the credit count, is the binding selection filter here.

programme_name_exact: MA in Screenwriting for Film + Television

No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment.

RPL route for applicants without a primary degree who have 4+ years relevant experience. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. Subject fit: a Business Intelligence licence would need to be argued under "Communication and Information Technology".

Grade II applicants may be considered via Recognition of Prior Learning. No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. FLAG: the degree must be "in the Humanities" - a Business Intelligence licence is outside that subject envelope, so subject eligibility is a bigger obstacle here than credit volume.

Minimum entry requirements: "QQI Level 8 degree or equivalent, H2.2. GPA 3.0 or equivalent international qualification." No credit figure given; states "Level 8 honours degree or equivalent"; Irish Level 8 is normally 240 ECTS, so a 180-ECTS licence requires individual equivalency assessment. BRIDGING ROUTE PUBLISHED: applicants holding a Level 7 (ordinary, 180-credit) degree at Merit 1 may enter the Postgraduate Diploma instead, with progression to the MA on achieving 60% in coursework - i.e. Galway explicitly offers a sub-Level-8 pathway, which is the closest published analogue to a 180-ECTS entrant and can add up to a year. Also requires a graded academic essay or 1,000-word film review plus personal statement; IELTS 7.0.

programme_name_exact: Master of Science in Creative Digital Media (Creative Digital Media and UX) - TU294
entry_requirement_note: Minimum entry requirements: "Honours bachelor degree (2.2 grade or higher) in any discipline relevant to multimedia authoring, design, production, architecture, humanities or computer science." A Statement of Purpose is required and "satisfying the minimum entry requirement is not a guarantee of a place". IELTS (Academic) 7.0 for international applicants.
